interest: Shows the Depression-era decline of Japan's geisha industry amid Western dance halls, and 1940 US caution over a table-tennis invite.
overview: Docket (1931-40): a report on the Depression-hit geisha industry losing ground to Western dance halls, and a 1940 query on accepting a Japanese table-tennis invitation amid strained relations.

subfiles.about: An extract from an embassy report detailing the severe economic decline of the Japanese geisha profession due to the Great Depression and Western cultural competition.
subfiles.summary: 1931 report: Japan's geisha industry, hit by the Depression and Western-style cafes, shrank to 80,717 geisha nationwide, forcing many to pawn kimonos.
subfiles.title: Report extract on hard times in the geisha industry

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet concerning a Department of State letter regarding U.S.-Japan relations and participation in a table tennis competition.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference (1940): State weighs whether US-Japan relations should affect accepting Japan's table-tennis invitation.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet regarding Japan Table Tennis Association invitation
